hints: Define time $t$ from the moment $B$ passes $O$ ($t = 0$ when $B$ is at $O$).
At $t = 0$, particle $A$ has already been moving past $O$ for $2\text{ s}$ at $10\text{ m s}^{-1}$, so its initial position is $s_{A0} = 10 \times 2 = 20\text{ m}$.
Since $A$ continues at constant speed $10\text{ m s}^{-1}$, its displacement is $s_A = 20 + 10t$.
For particle $B$, use $s = ut + \frac{1}{2}at^2$ with $u = 16\text{ m s}^{-1}$ and $a = -2\text{ m s}^{-2}$ to obtain $s_B = 16t - t^2$.
walkthrough:
Determine the displacement of particle $A$ at the moment $B$ passes through $O$ ($t = 0$), given that $A$ passed $O$ two seconds earlier at a constant speed of $10\text{ m s}^{-1}$:
$$s_A(0) = 10 \times 2 = 20\text{ m}$$
$$s_A(t) = 20 + 10t$$

Use the constant-acceleration formula $s = ut + \frac{1}{2}at^2$ for particle $B$, which passes $O$ at $t = 0$ with initial speed $u = 16\text{ m s}^{-1}$ and acceleration $a = -2\text{ m s}^{-2}$:
$$s_B(t) = 16t + \frac{1}{2}(-2)t^2 = 16t - t^2$$
teacher_walkthrough: Identify the time variable: $t$ represents the time in seconds after particle $B$ passes point $O$. Therefore, at $t = 0$, particle $B$ is at $O$, meaning $s_B(0) = 0$.

Determine the position of particle $A$ at $t = 0$. Since particle $A$ passed through $O$ $2\text{ seconds}$ before $B$, it has already travelled for $2\text{ s}$ at a constant speed of $10\text{ m s}^{-1}$:
$$s_A(0) = 10 \times 2 = 20\text{ m}$$

Because particle $A$ continues at constant velocity $10\text{ m s}^{-1}$, its displacement from $O$ after an additional $t$ seconds is:
$$s_A(t) = 20 + 10t$$

State the SUVAT displacement formula for particle $B$ under constant acceleration:
$$s = ut + \frac{1}{2}at^2$$

Substitute the initial speed $u = 16\text{ m s}^{-1}$ and deceleration $2\text{ m s}^{-2}$ (so $a = -2\text{ m s}^{-2}$):
$$s_B(t) = 16t + \frac{1}{2}(-2)t^2 = 16t - t^2$$

ai_rubric.Modelling Piecewise Motion: Forms $s_A = 20 + 10t$ and $s_B = 16t - t^2$ measuring time $t$ from when $B$ passes $O$.

hints: Find the time when particle $B$ comes to instantaneous rest by setting its velocity $v_B = u + at = 16 - 2t = 0$.
Substitute $t = 8\text{ s}$ into both displacement expressions $s_A(t)$ and $s_B(t)$ found in part (i).
walkthrough:
Find the time when particle $B$ comes to instantaneous rest using $v = u + at$ with $u = 16\text{ m s}^{-1}$ and $a = -2\text{ m s}^{-2}$:
$$v_B = 16 - 2t = 0 \implies 2t = 16 \implies t = 8\text{ s}$$

Calculate the displacement of each particle from $O$ at $t = 8\text{ s}$:
$$s_A(8) = 20 + 10(8) = 20 + 80 = 100\text{ m}$$
$$s_B(8) = 16(8) - (8)^2 = 128 - 64 = 64\text{ m}$$

Calculate the distance between the two particles at $t = 8\text{ s}$:
$$\text{Distance} = s_A(8) - s_B(8) = 100 - 64 = 36\text{ m}$$
teacher_walkthrough:
Recall that instantaneous rest occurs when the velocity of the particle is zero:
$$v_B = 0$$

Use the velocity equation for particle $B$, $v_B = u + at$ with $u = 16\text{ m s}^{-1}$ and $a = -2\text{ m s}^{-2}$:
$$16 - 2t = 0$$

Evaluate the displacement of particle $A$ at $t = 8\text{ s}$ using $s_A = 20 + 10t$:
$$s_A(8) = 20 + 10(8) = 20 + 80 = 100\text{ m}$$

Evaluate the displacement of particle $B$ at $t = 8\text{ s}$ using $s_B = 16t - t^2$:
$$s_B(8) = 16(8) - 8^2 = 128 - 64 = 64\text{ m}$$

Find the distance between the two particles by taking the difference of their positions:
$$\text{Distance} = s_A(8) - s_B(8) = 100 - 64 = 36\text{ m}$$

ai_rubric.Modelling Piecewise Motion: Solves $16 - 2t = 0 \implies t = 8\text{ s}$, evaluates $s_A(8) = 100\text{ m}$ and $s_B(8) = 64\text{ m}$, and finds distance $s_A - s_B = 36\text{ m}$.

hints: Express the separation distance function as $D(t) = s_A(t) - s_B(t) = (20 + 10t) - (16t - t^2) = t^2 - 6t + 20$.
To find the minimum separation, differentiate with respect to $t$ and set the derivative to zero: $\frac{dD}{dt} = 2t - 6 = 0$ (or complete the square).
Solve $2t - 6 = 0 \implies t = 3\text{ s}$, which corresponds to the moment when both particles have equal speeds.
Substitute $t = 3\text{ s}$ into $D(t)$ to calculate the minimum distance.
walkthrough:
Write the expression for the separation distance $D(t) = s_A(t) - s_B(t)$ between the particles:
$$D(t) = (20 + 10t) - (16t - t^2) = t^2 - 6t + 20$$

Find the stationary point by differentiating $D(t)$ with respect to $t$ and setting the derivative equal to zero:
$$\frac{dD}{dt} = 2t - 6 = 0 \implies 2t = 6 \implies t = 3\text{ s}$$

Evaluate the minimum distance at $t = 3\text{ s}$:
$$D(3) = 3^2 - 6(3) + 20 = 9 - 18 + 20 = 11\text{ m}$$
teacher_walkthrough:
Form the function representing the distance between particle $A$ and particle $B$:
$$D(t) = s_A(t) - s_B(t)$$

Substitute the expressions for $s_A$ and $s_B$ from part (i):
$$D(t) = (20 + 10t) - (16t - t^2) = t^2 - 6t + 20$$

To minimize distance, set the derivative $\frac{dD}{dt}$ to zero (this is also the physical instant when both particles have identical velocities, $v_A = v_B$):
$$\frac{dD}{dt} = \frac{d}{dt}(t^2 - 6t + 20) = 2t - 6 = 0$$

Confirm this is a minimum using the second derivative:
$$\frac{d^2D}{dt^2} = 2 > 0 \quad (\text{local minimum})$$

Substitute $t = 3\text{ s}$ back into the separation formula $D(t) = t^2 - 6t + 20$:
$$D(3) = (3)^2 - 6(3) + 20 = 9 - 18 + 20 = 11\text{ m}$$

ai_rubric.Differentiating Motion Functions: Forms separation $s_A - s_B = t^2 - 6t + 20$, differentiates to find minimum at $t = 3$, and evaluates minimum distance as $11\text{ m}$.
